title: Articles
lede: Prototype history of the Pittsburgh & Ohio Valley, Pittsburgh Coke & Chemical, the rest of the POHC line, and the railroads of the Chartiers Valley.

items.title: Pittsburgh & Ohio Valley Railway
items.blurb: The steel-plant railroad HART succeeds, 1899–1994: what each job did, track names, typical moves, and locomotives, linked to the original posts and photos.

items.title: Voices of the P&OV
items.blurb: The crews, trainmasters, and clerks of the P&OV in Mark Connolly's words: sayings, yard-office life, Local 150, and the people remembered.

items.title: Neville Island coke, cement, and chemical history
items.blurb: American Steel & Wire through Davison, PC&C, Shenango, Calgon, Kosmos, and Aristech — pig iron to about 1990–91, coke to 2016.

items.title: Who became who: Neville Island plants
items.blurb: Coke and iron, cement, carbon, and chemicals, from American Steel & Wire to today, company by company, with a year-by-year table.

items.title: POHC line industries, McKees Rocks to Washington
items.blurb: Pressed Steel Car, Kirwan Heights, Canonsburg pottery and transformers, Washington Steel, and the other plants along Chartiers Creek.

items.title: Railroads of the Chartiers Valley
items.blurb: Chartiers Branch and PC&Y as two different railroads, then PIR and POHC, plus the Class I connections around McKees Rocks and Duff Junction.

items.title: The Kirwan Heights Industrial District
items.blurb: C. P. Mayer's industrial park on the PRR Chartiers Branch: Mayer Brick, Flannery Bolt staybolts, American Vanadium, Higbee Glass, and Universal Steel, 1903 into the 1950s.

items.title: Pittsburgh Coke & Chemical doubles pig iron (1951)
items.blurb: New York Times financial page, 6 July 1951: rights offering to raise Neville Island pig iron from 300,000 to 600,000 net tons a year.

items.title: Coraopolis Record: “Appreciate The Moment” and “Bring Back The Trolleys”
items.blurb: Two 2016–17 editorials from the revived Coraopolis Record: Dravo, Standard Steel and PC&C remaking the island, and the Route 23 trolley through Neville Island.
